terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo loads routes, pings ports and waits for a slow forecast, printing how long each took.

tasks.title: Load every route at once
tasks.description:
Implement `loadRoutes(ids, getRoute)` in `src/loadRoutes.js`. It returns a promise of the routes for every id, in the same order as `ids`.

- start every `getRoute(id)` call before waiting for any of them
- keep the order of `ids`, whatever order the answers arrive in
- if any call rejects, reject with that error
- `loadRoutes([])` resolves with `[]`

**Timing:** `getRoute` is a parameter that defaults to the fake service. The check passes a fake whose answers it settles one by one, in an order it chooses, and records which calls had started before any answer arrived.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.js` and read the first two lines.
Turn the list of ids into a list of promises.
Wait for all of them in one step.
Run the demo again: three routes should take about as long as the slowest one.
hints: Calling `getRoute` starts a request. You want every request started before any waiting happens.
`ids.map(...)` calls a function for every id straight away and gives you an array of whatever it returned.
`Promise.all` takes an array of promises and gives you one promise of their values, in the array's order. It rejects as soon as any of them rejects.

tasks.title: Which ports are answering
tasks.description:
Implement `portStatus(ports, ping)` in `src/portStatus.js`. It pings every port at the same time and resolves with `{ up, down }`.

- `up` is the list of ports whose `ping(port)` resolved
- `down` is a list of `{ port, reason }` for every port whose ping rejected, where `reason` is the error's `message`
- both lists keep the order of `ports`
- `portStatus` never rejects because a ping failed, even when every port is down

**Timing:** `ping` is a parameter that defaults to the fake service. The check passes a fake whose answers it settles in reverse order, and records which pings started before any answer arrived.
nextSteps: Start a ping for every port.
Wait for every ping to settle, successful or not.
Walk the results and sort each port into one of the two lists.
Run the demo: reef should be down.
hints: `Promise.all` gives up at the first failure, so it cannot tell you about the ports that answered.
`Promise.allSettled` never rejects. It resolves with one object per promise that has a `status`, plus `value` or `reason`.
The results come back in the same order as the promises, so result `i` belongs to `ports[i]`.

tasks.title: Give up after a while
tasks.description:
Implement `withTimeout(promise, ms, timers)` in `src/withTimeout.js`. It returns a promise that settles the same way as `promise`, unless `promise` takes longer than `ms`.

- start exactly one timer with `timers.setTimeout(callback, ms)`
- if the timer fires first, reject with an `Error` whose `name` is `'TimeoutError'` and whose message contains `ms`, such as `'Timed out after 500 ms'`
- if `promise` settles first, settle the same way and call `timers.clearTimeout` with the timer's id
- if `promise` rejects after the timeout, that rejection must not be left unhandled

**Timing:** `timers` is `{ setTimeout, clearTimeout }` and defaults to the real ones. The check passes a fake clock: it records the delay you ask for and whether you clear the timer, and fires it by hand, so no real time passes.
nextSteps: Build a promise that rejects when the timer fires.
Let it race against the promise you were given.
Clear the timer once the race is over.
Run the demo: one forecast arrives, the other times out after 500 ms.
hints: You need two promises competing: the real work, and one that only ever rejects, after `ms`.
`Promise.race` settles the same way as whichever promise settles first, and keeps listening to the others, so a late failure is not unhandled.
Keep the id that `setTimeout` returns in a variable. `.finally(...)` on the raced promise is a tidy place to clear it, whichever way the race ended.
